ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$ passes through points A, B ($-3$, $0$), and C ($0$, $3$). Find the analytic equation of the parabola.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the parabola $y=-x^2+bx+c$ passes through points A, B $(-3,0)$, and C $(0,3)$. Find the analytic equation of the parabola.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Substitute B $(-3,0)$ and C $(0,3)$ into $y=-x^2+bx+c$, yielding \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -9-3b+c=0 \\ c=3 \end{array} \right. \] Therefore, \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b=-2 \\ c=3 \end{array} \right. \] Therefore, the equation of the parabola is $\boxed{y=-x^2-2x+3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Substitute B $(-3,0)$ and C $(0,3)$ into $y=-x^2+bx+c$, yielding \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -9-3b+c=0 \\ c=3 \end{array} \right. \] Therefore, \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b=-2 \\ c=3 \end{array} \right. \] Therefore, the equation of the parabola is $\boxed{y=-x^2-2x+3}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a plane rectangular coordinate system, and the parabola opens downward; it intersects the x-axis on the left side at point B, on the right side at point A, and intersects the y-axis at point C. The figure also uses a dashed line to mark the axis of symmetry near the vertex. Reasoning: It is known that the parabola is y = -x^2 + bx + c, and it passes through B(-3,0) and C(0,3). Substitute C(0,3), obtaining 3 = c, so c = 3. Substitute B(-3,0), obtaining 0 = -(-3)^2 + b(-3) + c = -9 - 3b + c. Substitute c = 3, obtaining -9 - 3b + 3 = 0, that is, -6 - 3b = 0, so b = -2. Therefore the analytic expression of the parabola is y = -x^2 - 2x + 3.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the graph shows a downward-opening parabola with two x-intercepts, labeled B on the left and A on the right, and a y-intercept labeled C. From the text, note that the leading coefficient is -1 and B(-3,0), C(0,3) lie on the parabola. Since B is an x-intercept, x=-3 is a root. Write the parabola in factored form as y=-(x+3)(x-r), where r is the other x-intercept. Use the y-intercept C(0,3): 3=-(0+3)(0-r)=3r, so r=1. Expand y=-(x+3)(x-1) to obtain y=-x^2-2x+3.
